'''Jaime Jaquez Jr.''' ({{IPAc-en|'|h|aɪ|m|eɪ|_|'|h|ɑː|k|ɛ|z}}, {{respell|HY|may|_|HAH|kez}}; born February 18, 2001) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]] of the [[Pac-12 Conference]]. He was named a consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and voted the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]] as a [[senior (education)|senior]] in 2023. Jaquez has earned three [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] selections, including first-team honors twice. He is also a two-time member of the Pac-12 All-Defensive Team.

==Early life and high school career==
Jaquez is the son of Angela and Jaime Jaquez Sr., who met while playing basketball at [[Concordia University Irvine|Concordia University]].<ref name="bolch">{{cite news |last1=Bolch |first1=Ben |title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. giving Mick Cronin what he wants for UCLA's rebuild |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2019-11-28/jaime-jaquez-jr-giving-mick-cronin-what-he-wants-for-ucla-rebuild |accessdate=April 2, 2020 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=November 28, 2019}}</ref> Jaime Jr. is the third generation of his family to have played college basketball; Jaime Sr.'s father, Ezequiel, who came to California with his family from Mexico as a child, played at Ventura Community College and [[Northern Arizona Lumberjacks men's basketball|Northern Arizona University]].<ref name=Legacy>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35755017/the-third-generation-basketball-legacy-ucla-gabriela-jaime-jaquez-jr |title=The third-generation basketball legacy of UCLA's Gabriela and Jaime Jaquez Jr. |first=Myron |last=Medcalf |website=ESPN.com |date=March 3, 2023 |access-date=March 3, 2023}}</ref>

Jaime Jr. was born in [[Irvine, California]], and has a younger brother Marcos and younger sister Gabriela. Jaquez grew up in [[Camarillo, California|Camarillo]] and attended [[Camarillo High School]]. As a [[freshman]], he averaged 15.3 points, 10.0 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], 2.3 [[assist (basketball)|assists]], and 2.6 [[steal (basketball)|steals]] per game and led the team to a 25–7 record and the [[California Interscholastic Federation]] (CIF) semifinals. As a [[sophomore]], Jaquez earned all-[[Ventura County, California|Ventura County]] second-team honors, averaging 24.1 points, 10.9 rebounds, 2.2 assists, and 2.6 steals per game, despite missing 12 games with an ankle injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. |url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/j/jaquez-jr-jaime.aspx |website=[[USA Basketball]] |accessdate=April 2, 2020}}</ref>

Jaquez averaged 31.7 points, 11.7 rebounds, 3.7 assists, and 2.1 steals per game as a [[senior (education)|senior]] and helped the team finish 25–4 and win its first Coastal Canyon League title.<ref name="ledin">{{cite news |last1=Ledin |first1=Loren |title=Camarillo's Jaime Jaquez Jr. is The Star's Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://www.vcstar.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2019/03/16/camarillos-jaquez-jr-stars-boys-basketball-player-year/3098491002/ |accessdate=April 2, 2020 |work=[[Ventura County Star]] |date=March 16, 2019}}</ref> He earned first-team All-CIF Southern Section honors and finished his high school career with 2,653 points.<ref name="tay">{{cite news |last1=Tay |first1=Jared |title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. hopes to make familia proud, aims to inspire future Latino players |url=https://dailybruin.com/2020/02/28/jaime-jaquez-jr-hopes-to-make-familia-proud-aims-to-inspire-future-latino-players/ |accessdate=April 2, 2020 |work=The Daily Bruin |date=February 28, 2020}}</ref> Jaquez broke the school single-game scoring record with a 54-point outing against [[Royal High School (California)|Royal High School]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gomez |first1=Eric |title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. eyes hoop dreams at UCLA, Mexico, PanAms |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/27287297/jaime-jaquez-jr-eyes-hoop-dreams-ucla-mexico-panams |accessdate=April 2, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=July 31, 2019}}</ref> Jaquez was also a [[pitcher (baseball)|pitcher]] on the high school [[baseball]] team.<ref name="ledin" />

==College career==
[[File:Jaime Jaquez Jr.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Jaquez in 2019]]
At the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], Jaquez became a starter for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|Bruins]] during [[2019 Maui Invitational Tournament|the Maui Jim Maui Invitational]] in November 2019.<ref name="tay" /> He scored 17 points and had 12 rebounds in a win against [[Chaminade Silverswords men's basketball|Chaminade]] on November 26.<ref name=bolch/> On December 1, he scored a season-high 18 points in a 93–64 win over [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Jose State]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Jaquez, Hill lead UCLA to 93–64 win over San Jose State |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401170605 |accessdate=April 2, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 1, 2019}}</ref> He scored 18 points on February 27, 2020, and hit the game-winning three-pointer with 0.6 seconds remaining in a 75–72 win over [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Vanoni |first1=Maggie |title=Jaime Jaquez Jr.'s shot lifts UCLA men's basketball into first-place tie in Pac-12 |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2020/02/27/jaime-jaquez-jr-s-shot-lifts-ucla-mens-basketball-into-first-place-tie-in-pac-12/ |accessdate=April 2, 2020 |work=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |date=February 27, 2020}}</ref> As a freshman, Jaquez averaged 8.9 points and 4.8 rebounds per game. He was named honorable mention [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]] All-Freshman team.<ref>{{cite news |title=Factoids on UCLA Hoops Heading into Pac-12 Tourney |url=https://247sports.com/college/ucla/Article/UCLA-Bruins-Basketball-UCLA-Basketball-News-and-Notes-144831374/ |accessdate=March 30, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=March 11, 2020}}</ref>

On February 18, 2021, Jaquez scored 25 points on his 20th birthday in a 74–60 win over [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], the Bruins' fifth straight in [[Arizona–UCLA men's basketball rivalry|its rivalry with the Wildcats]].<ref>{{cite news|title=UCLA beats Arizona 74-60 to complete sweep of Wildcats|date=February 18, 2021|website=ESPN.com|agency=AP|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401265426|access-date=February 19, 2021}}</ref> For the season, he was a second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] selection and was named to the Pac-12 All-Defensive Team.<ref>{{cite news|first=Tarek|last=Fattal|title=UCLA PG Tyger Campbell earns Pac-12 first-team honors|date=March 9, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2021/03/09/ucla-pg-tyger-campbell-earns-pac-12-first-team-honors/|access-date=March 10, 2021}}</ref> In UCLA's [[First Four]] play-in game of the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2021 NCAA tournament]], he led the Bruins in scoring with a 27 points in a 86–80 overtime win against [[Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball|Michigan State]].<ref>"[https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-03-18/ucla-michigan-state-first-four-ncaa-tournament UCLA Surges Late to Save Season and Defeat Michigan State in First Four Thriller]" ''Los Angeles Times. March 18, 2021.'' Retrieved March 18, 2021.</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=UCLA beats Michigan St 86-80 in overtime in First Four game|date=March 19, 2021|website=CBSSports.com|agency=AP|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/gametracker/recap/NCAAB_20210318_UCLA@MICHST/|access-date=March 19, 2021}}</ref> UCLA advanced to the [[Final Four]], losing to [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]].<ref name=bolch_04062023>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. declares for the NBA draft, will forgo year of eligibility|date=April 6, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-04-06/ucla-star-jaime-jaquez-jr-declares-nba-draft|access-date=May 8, 2023}}</ref>

Mary's]], but exited the game and did not return after spraining his right ankle with seven minutes remaining in the second half.<ref name=bolch_03232022/><ref>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA defeats St. Mary’s to return to the Sweet 16 for the second straight year|date=March 19, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-03-19/ucla-defeats-saint-marys-ncaa-tournament-march-madness-sweet-16|access-date=March 19, 2022}}</ref> He was averaging 20.5 points in his Jaquez returned to UCLA for his senior year in [[2022–23 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2022–23]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. will return to UCLA in hopes of winning a national title|date=April 18, 2022|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-04-18/jaime-jaquez-announces-he-will-return-ucla-basketball|access-date=February 24, 2023}}</ref> For the second straight season, he was named to a finalist for the Julius Erving Award.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaquez Jr. Among Five Finalists for Julius Erving Award|date=March 8, 2023|publisher=UCLA Athletics|url=https://uclabruins.com/news/2023/3/8/mens-basketball-jaquez-jr-among-five-finalists-for-julius-erving-award.aspx|access-date=March 15, 2023}}</ref> On February 4, 2023, he had a game-high 24 points and a career-high 15 rebounds in a 76–52 win over [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. powers No. 9 UCLA in a get-well rout of Washington State|date=February 4, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-02-04/ucla-beats-washington-state-jaime-jaquez-jr-recap|access-date=February 24, 2023}}</ref> That month, he scored late baskets in multiple games to help lead the team to victories, including seven points in {{frac|3|1|2}} minutes as the Bruins secured a win over [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Why UCLA’s Jaime Jaquez Jr. is in race for Pac-12 player of year|date=February 24, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-02-24/ucla-basketball-jaime-jaquez-jr-in-player-of-year-race|access-date=February 26, 2023}}</ref> He led UCLA to their first Pac-12 regular season title since [[2012–13 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2013]].<ref name=fattal_03072023>{{cite web|first=Tarek|last=Fattal|title=UCLA’s Jaime Jaquez Jr. named Pac-12 Player of the Year|date=March 7, 2023|work=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2023/03/07/uclas-jaime-jaquez-jr-named-pac-12-player-of-the-year/|access-date=March 8, 2023}}</ref> The Bruins received a No. 2 seed in the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2023 NCAA tournament]]. In the opener, Jaquez had 17 points, eight rebounds, and a career-high five steals in a 86–53 rout over No. 15-seed [[UNC Asheville Bulldogs men's basketball|UNC Asheville]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title==UCLA dodges upset trend, opens NCAA tournament with rout of UNC Asheville|date=March 16, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-16/ucla-vs-unc-asheville-ncaa-tournament-recap|access-date=March 18, 2023}}</ref> UCLA again reached the Sweet Sixteen, losing again in the tournament to Gonzaga. For the season, he averaged 17.8 points and 8.2 rebounds.<ref name=bolch_04062023/> He was named a consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]],<ref>{{cite press release|title=Pac-12 Men's Basketball Weekly Rundown - March 15, 2023|date=March 15, 2023|publisher=Pac-12 Conference|url=https://pac-12.com/article/2023/03/15/pac-12-mens-basketball-weekly-rundown-march-15-2023|access-date=March 16, 2023}}</ref> and  received the [[Lute Olson Award]] as the college player of the year.<ref name=bolch_04062023/> Jaquez was voted the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]], becoming the first Bruin to win since [[Kevin Love]] in [[2007–08 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2008]] and the first UCLA senior to capture the award since [[Ed O'Bannon]] in [[1994–95 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|1995]].<ref name=pac12_03072023>{{cite press release|title=2022-23 Pac-12 Men's Basketball All-Conference honors and Annual Performance Awards, presented by Nextiva|date=March 7, 2023|publisher=Pac-12 Conference|url=https://pac-12.com/article/2023/03/07/2022-23-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-honors-and-annual-performance|access-date=March 7, 2023}}</ref> He also earned his second consecutive first-team all-conference selection.<ref name=fattal_03072023/> After the season, Jaquez declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]], forgoing the extra year of eligibility that was available due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]]. He ended his career ranked eighth in UCLA history in career scoring (1,802) and career steals (178) and ninth in total games played (134).<ref>{{cite web|title=UCLA’s Jaime Jaquez Jr. declares for NBA draft|date=April 6, 2023|publisher=Associated Press|url=https://apnews.com/article/ucla-jaime-jaquez-nba-draft-498c43c4a09c2e4665cbc959b198f45e|access-date=May 8, 2023}}</ref>

==National team career==
Jaquez played for the [[Mexico men's national basketball team|Mexico national team]] in the [[Basketball at the 2019 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|2019 Pan American Games]] in Lima, Peru.<ref name="tay" />
